note: The four session authentication payloads as spec/wire.md section 1.1 and spec/session.cddl define them, frame envelope included. Encoders must match every canonical case byte for byte. tools/validate_session_vectors.py reimplements the rules from the specification and cross-checks them against the Rust codec. Every case here is one whole frame: bytes past the length the envelope declares are a caller mistake rather than a payload, and are covered by the oracle's own unit test instead.

canonical.name: auth_context_requires_no_authentication
canonical.note: No capability format advertised, which spec/wire.md section 1.1 gives as the way a deployment says it requires no authentication.

canonical.name: auth_context_proof_of_possession
canonical.note: Formats ascend and never repeat, so one server policy has one encoding.

canonical.name: auth_context_unbound_bearer
canonical.note: A capability with no channel binding, which spec/security.md section 5 allows only where policy declares the shorter lifetime and the replay exposure it costs.

canonical.name: auth_context_longest_nonce
canonical.note: The nonce bound and the format bound each admit their own maximum.

canonical.name: session_open_minimal
canonical.note: An empty requested scope asks for the capability's whole scope.

canonical.name: session_open_bound_capability
canonical.note: A capability bound by proof of possession, with a scope narrower than the capability's own.

canonical.name: session_accept_narrowed_scope
canonical.note: The granted scope may be narrower than what was requested.

canonical.name: session_reject_authorization_failed
canonical.note: An empty detail, which is what a server sends when any detail would be an oracle.

canonical.name: session_reject_authentication_failed
canonical.note: The third of the three reasons a rejection may carry, so every one of them is frozen here.

canonical.name: session_reject_replay
canonical.note: A registered reason and a bounded UTF-8 detail.

rejected.name: nonce_shorter_than_the_bound
rejected.note: A nonce below 16 bytes has less freshness than the exchange assumes.

rejected.name: nonce_longer_than_the_bound
rejected.note: Refused by length before the value is examined.

rejected.name: formats_out_of_order
rejected.note: Descending formats would give one server policy two encodings.

rejected.name: unknown_binding
rejected.note: Only none and proof of possession are defined.

rejected.name: unknown_format_version
rejected.note: A version this endpoint does not implement is refused rather than guessed at.

rejected.name: non_canonical_length_head
rejected.note: RFC 8949 core deterministic encoding requires the shortest head that fits.

rejected.name: trailing_bytes_inside_the_payload
rejected.note: A payload longer than its own structure is malformed, not ignored.

rejected.name: capability_format_zero
rejected.note: A client cannot name the reserved format.

rejected.name: capability_format_above_the_registry
rejected.note: The registry is two bytes wide.

rejected.name: unregistered_reject_reason
rejected.note: A rejection reports an authentication or authorization outcome, not any error code.
